result:
All downloads are recorded per R3, and everything downloaded lives inside PLAYGROUND. The run is complete.

## Done — master validator returned PASS

`output/hw_20261008_5ae5f8/final/main.pdf`, 11 pages, all ten exercises, 100/100 points. Used 3 of 5 submission rounds.

**How the assignment was cut.** Ten exercises into five workers, on dependence rather than numbering. The one substantive merge was **Ex. 3.3–3.8 into a single worker**: Ex. 3.8 defines the algorithms that 3.4/3.5/3.6 argue about, and 3.3 and 3.7 are two halves of the same page-fault service routine. Split across workers, the document would have carried two incompatible accounts of what NFU's counter does. Ex. 3.9 and 3.10 were deliberately *not* merged — their only coupling is "don't pick the same papers", which I enforced by writing p5's brief only after p4 reported its three picks, then naming them as forbidden.

**The reading trap worth knowing about.** The paper list's topic column uses merged cells. The CSV export puts "Memory Management" on row 3-1 only and leaves 3-2…3-7 blank, so counting rows that literally say it finds one paper instead of seven; the PDF text channel is worse, extracting column-major and dumping paper 3-6's title at the bottom of the page, which makes the group look like six. The page image plus the `3-` ID prefix settled it independently. I put all of that in p4's brief rather than letting the worker rediscover it.

**Two things I got wrong, both corrected.**

The first cost a session: I ended a turn while `fw spawn-worker` was in the background, and the sandbox tore the PID namespace down with it, killing p2 mid-validation. After that I held every wait in the foreground. A second interruption was different — the master hit its own 120-minute wall limit.

The second is worth flagging because it nearly shipped. The validator's round-1 report said a Pond citation fused two statements. I checked by grepping the paper for `stranded`, found support, and "fixed" the sentence — but the decisive sentence uses `stranding`, so my search couldn't have falsified the claim. The original wording was correct; my edit introduced a misattribution. The validator withdrew its own finding in round 2, I verified at the source properly, and reverted. That cost a submission round and is exactly the R9 failure mode the spec warns about, committed while trying to fix an R9 defect.

**Knowingly left in:** `main.tex` has no `\author`, so LaTeX emits "No \author given". Nothing in specs.md or the assignment asks for a name and I have none to use — putting the git account's name on a homework submission isn't my call to make. The warning never reaches the PDF.

**One environment substitution, per env.md:** `\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}` alone demanded EC bitmap fonts that Metafont can't generate against a read-only `~/.TinyTeX`. Added `\usepackage{lmodern}` (installed, scalable Type1) ahead of it.
